title: Taxes and Executive Pay: Evidence from Nonqualified Deferred Compensation
eligible_reason: Not staggered. The tax change (CFO compensation becoming deductible under Section 162(m)) has one common date: cforeg2009 = cfo x regulation2009, and regulation2009 = 1 exactly for fiscal years 2009-2010 for every firm (firsttest.dta: years 2006, 2007 = 0; 2009, 2010 = 1; 2008 absent). The design compares CFOs with CEOs/other executives in the same firm around one date. Every column also includes time-varying firm and executive controls (logat, btm, leverage, ret, idvol, logcomp, logtenure, statetax, etc.).
design_notes: Executive-year panel (CFO vs. CEO / highest-paid other executive) of S&P firms; reghdfe logdefer_w cforeg2009 + controls, absorb(year cfofirm) with cfofirm = firm x executive; clustered by firm. Table 6 (m162 on cfopost) and Table 7 (logcomp on treat x regulation2009, firm and year FE) use the same 2009 date.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: regulation2009 = 1 for fiscal years 2009-2010 for all firms (verified in firsttest.dta).
data_files_note: readme.txt: hand-collected deferred-compensation data withheld for future work; the package ships 'a subsample of firms in the S&P 500 index' (firsttest.dta: 912 rows, 150 firms).
data_provenance_note: Non-random subsample of the original data (S&P 500 firms only); closest category is random_subsample. Moot because the design is not staggered.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Single 2009 policy date; executive-level 2x2 DiD with controls.
